briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Governor's Race Turns Pro-Cannabis in Michigan as Psychedelics Break Through Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan operators just got a campaign-trail champion: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is pledging to gut the state's 24% wholesale tax while courting industry cash, even as demand holds steady and new hospitality-forward stores push the market upmarket. Nationally, Compass Pathways' accelerated FDA pathway and a maturing DEA rescheduling hearing signal psychedelics and cannabis are both closer to the mainstream than ever.

local.text: Michigan's governor's race just became a cannabis-tax referendum: Republican nominee John James is proposing to 'repeal or sharply reduce' the 24% wholesale tax and is actively courting industry donors, while Democrat Jocelyn Benson has yet to stake out a firm position.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is building a fully integrated cannabis hospitality model — retail, on-site consumption, dining and event licensing under one roof — in a bet that a winery-style elevated experience can command higher price points, with a fall opening on tap.

Jars Cannabis notched a win for operators statewide after Madison Heights removed a Flock surveillance camera aimed at its parking lot, capping a public standoff that started when the retailer posted a 'No Flock Zone' sign to block the lens.

The demand story is holding up: after a soft January, statewide sales climbed back to $255.4 million by March and held relatively steady through June at $253.5 million, with the tax hit landing mostly on wholesale margins rather than consumer wallets.

The hard number giving repeal advocates ammunition: the 24% wholesale tax generated only about $37 million in Q2 2026 and $34 million in Q1 — against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter — momentum a Republican lawmaker is riding with a formal repeal bill, HB 6224.

national.text: Compass Pathways just accelerated its psilocybin timeline: the FDA granted a rolling NDA review and awarded COMP360 a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for treatment-resistant depression, while fresh 26-week Phase 3 data confirmed the drug's rapid onset and durable response.

The federal marijuana rescheduling case is no longer stuck in neutral — the DEA administrative hearing reached its closing-argument stage in late August, a real procedural milestone toward Schedule III.

The FDA's newly finalized psychedelics guidance signals the agency is 'receptive' to helping companies succeed, with Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy now positioned for possible approval as early as this year following Trump's executive order clearing a path for psilocybin, MDMA and ibogaine.

Consolidation is creating winners: Vireo Growth completed its acquisition of 17 PharmaCann Colorado dispensaries for roughly $49 million in stock and assumed liabilities, expanding its Colorado retail footprint to 56 locations.

Not every deal is a win — Advanced Flower Capital's loan to Justice Grown is in maturity default with roughly $78.8 million outstanding, and AFC has begun Article 9 foreclosures on Pennsylvania and New Jersey assets, the kind of distressed inventory that well-capitalized operators are already circling.
